igcse-ict-c1.story: The city hospital is getting brand-new technology. Learn how each system works and help set it up, Dr. {name}.

igcse-ict-c1-u1.intro: The theatre's new screens can be controlled by voice and gesture. Learn how these controls work.
igcse-ict-c1-u1.why: Sterile gloves make touching a normal screen tricky during an operation, so some operating theatres use voice or gesture control to work hands-free.

igcse-ict-c1-u3.why: Doctors can check test results on a tablet at the bedside and get urgent alerts on a smartphone.

igcse-ict-c1-u4.intro: The lab's new AI helps read scans. Learn what AI is good at, and where a doctor is still needed.
igcse-ict-c1-u4.why: AI can help doctors spot signs of illness in X-rays and scans, and a doctor usually checks the result and makes the final decision.

igcse-ict-c1-u5.intro: Trainees practise here before working with real patients. Learn how AR and VR make that possible.
igcse-ict-c1-u5.why: Trainee doctors can practise an operation in VR many times before they ever help with a real one.

cls9-phys-c11-u1.intro: Why does a giant hospital ship float while a tiny coin sinks? Find out.
cls9-phys-c11-u1.why: Bone is denser than muscle and fat is less dense, so scans can tell them apart. Density matters in medicine too.

cls9-phys-c11-u2.intro: Is this medicine ingredient real or fake? Density can tell.
cls9-phys-c11-u2.why: Labs check that ingredients are genuine. Measuring density is one simple test.

igcse-ict-c1.story: The city's control systems are getting a big upgrade, and you're on the build team, Engineer {name}.

igcse-ict-c1-u1.intro: The new control room uses voice commands and gestures. Learn how they work, and when they don't.
igcse-ict-c1-u1.why: With gloves on and hands full, an engineer can check a plan by voice or gesture. But on a noisy site, voice control can mishear: a real disadvantage.

igcse-ict-c1-u2.intro: Big design jobs and site visits need different computers. Pick the right one.
igcse-ict-c1-u2.why: Heavy 3D design often runs on a powerful desktop in the office, while a laptop can go to the site to show the client.

igcse-ict-c1-u3.intro: Out on site, mobile devices are part of your toolkit. Find out what each one does best.
igcse-ict-c1-u3.why: A tablet can show the plans on site, and a phone photo of a problem can reach the team in seconds.

igcse-ict-c1-u4.intro: The workshop's robots need a smart brain. Learn how AI works and where it has limits.
igcse-ict-c1-u4.why: Engineers design robots and smart systems that can use AI to spot faults before a machine breaks down.

igcse-ict-c1-u5.intro: See the building before it's built. Learn how AR and VR help engineers plan.
igcse-ict-c1-u5.why: With AR, an engineer can point a tablet at an empty room and see where the walls and pipes will go.

igcse-ict-c1.story: The space base is preparing for a new mission. Get every system ready, Astronaut {name}.

igcse-ict-c1-u1.intro: Mission Control is testing voice and gesture controls. Learn how these interfaces work.
igcse-ict-c1-u1.why: Spacesuit gloves are thick, so small buttons are hard to press. Voice control is being tested to help astronauts work hands-free.

igcse-ict-c1-u2.intro: Some computers stay on the ground and some fly. Decide which computer goes where.
igcse-ict-c1-u2.why: Mission Control uses big desktop workstations, while astronauts take laptops up to the space station.

igcse-ict-c1-u3.intro: On the station, every device must earn its place. Find out what phones and tablets do best.
igcse-ict-c1-u3.why: Astronauts have used tablets to read step-by-step instructions while their hands do the work.

igcse-ict-c1-u4.intro: The rover must drive a long way from home. Learn what AI can and can't do.
igcse-ict-c1-u4.why: Mars is so far away that signals take minutes to arrive, so rovers can steer around nearby rocks on their own while the team on Earth plans the route.

igcse-ict-c1-u5.intro: Before any spacewalk, astronauts rehearse. Learn how AR and VR help them train.
igcse-ict-c1-u5.why: Astronauts practise spacewalks in VR before they ever step outside the station.

cls9-phys-c11-u1.why: Saturn's average density is less than water's. If you found a big enough bathtub, Saturn would float in it!

cls9-phys-c11-u2.intro: How do you measure the density of the Earth or the Sun without a giant scale? Ask the scientists.

igcse-ict-c1.story: The underwater research station is getting new technology. Dive in and set up each system, Diver {name}.

igcse-ict-c1-u1.intro: Divers already talk with their hands. Learn how computers understand voice and gestures.

igcse-ict-c1-u2.intro: The ship's lab needs the right computers on board. Choose the best one for each job.

igcse-ict-c1-u3.intro: On the boat, small devices do big jobs. Find out what phones and tablets are best at.
igcse-ict-c1-u3.why: In a waterproof case, a tablet can show the dive plan and a fish chart, and a phone on the boat can record where each dive site is.

igcse-ict-c1-u4.intro: Robots explore where divers can't go. Learn how AI helps them.
igcse-ict-c1-u4.why: Underwater robots can use AI to map the seabed and recognise fish and coral in thousands of photos.

igcse-ict-c1-u5.intro: Explore a shipwreck without getting wet. Learn the difference between AR and VR.
igcse-ict-c1-u5.why: VR lets you explore a shipwreck from home, and special AR masks can show divers their depth and direction.
